passage: Irawati lay on her bed in the third-floor flat. In the hall, her father Asif was telling his brother on the phone that she would "take first rank again this year." She had come second last time. Her pencil box sat on the desk and a small ugly thought came: what if she made sure of first rank some other way? Her throat felt tight. She wiped her face, walked into the hall and said, "Papa, when you say first rank every day, I get scared. I don't want to come second." Asif put down the phone. "I didn't know it felt that heavy," he said, and sat beside her.

qa.q: Who was Asif talking to on the phone?
qa.a: He was talking to his brother.

qa.q: What was Irawati feeling when the thought of making sure of first rank some other way came?
qa.a: She was frightened of coming second and disappointing her father; her tight throat and wiped face suggest she felt overwhelmed.

qa.q: What did Irawati do that worked, and why?
qa.a: She told Asif honestly how heavy the pressure felt, which opened a talk instead of leaving her alone with the idea; a lower honest score is safer than a high dishonest one 🙂.

qa.q: What is it like for Asif to hear this from Irawati?
qa.a: He seems surprised and concerned: he put down the phone and said he had not known it felt that heavy, so he may now be ready to listen.

grounding: Illustrates a child under parental demand for top rank who honestly tells her father the pressure instead of cheating.

passage:
'Rank one again this term, Yamini. Nothing less,' Papa said, not looking up from his newspaper.
Yamini's spoon stopped halfway to her mouth. 'Papa, what if I can't?'
'You can. Your cousin did.'
Later, in the kitchen, Yamini whispered to Usha Maasi, 'Some kids in my class have ways to see the answers. I thought maybe I could... just this once.'
Usha Maasi put down the knife. 'Because of Papa?'
'I can't breathe when he says rank one.'
'Then that's what you tell him. Not the cheating. The not breathing.'
'He'll be angry.'
'I'll sit with you.'
At dinner, Yamini's voice shook. 'Papa, when you say rank one, my chest feels squeezed. I'm scared enough to think about cheating. I'd rather get rank five honestly.'
Papa lowered his newspaper. For a long moment he said nothing. Then, 'I didn't know it was that heavy, beta.'

qa.q: How did Yamini feel when Papa said 'Nothing less'?
qa.a: Pressured and frightened; she felt she couldn't breathe and even thought about cheating.

qa.q: What did Usha Maasi advise, and why was it wise?
qa.a: To tell Papa honestly how heavy the pressure felt instead of cheating, since an honest lower rank is safer.

qa.q: How did Papa react when Yamini spoke?
qa.a: He was quiet, then admitted he hadn't known it was that heavy.

grounding: A girl under pressure to top the class tempted to cheat tells her father honestly how heavy it feels, with her aunt's support.

passage: In Class 6, my parents told me that if I didn't come first in the half-yearly exam, I'd have to leave dance class. I'm Afreen, and I remember that week as one long stomach ache. Jatin, from the next row, whispered that his cousin could get the answers in advance. For one whole night I thought about saying yes. Then I pictured Ammi finding out, and my stomach hurt even more. On Saturday I sat on the kitchen floor while Abbu was making tea and said, 'I'm so scared of not coming first that I nearly cheated.' He turned off the stove. He listened for a long time. That night he and Ammi said dance stays, whatever my rank. I came fourth. Honestly.

qa.q: What would Afreen have had to leave if not first?
How did Afreen feel that week?
qa.a: Anxious and pressured, as if the whole week were one long stomach ache.

qa.q: What did Afreen do instead of taking the answers?
qa.a: Told Abbu honestly about the fear and the near-cheating, and Abbu listened.

qa.q: How might Abbu have felt when he turned off the stove?
qa.a: Shocked and concerned, realising how much pressure Afreen felt.

grounding: A child pressured by parents to top the class nearly cheats, then tells a parent honestly how heavy the pressure is.
